_comment: Every listing ever seen. Dead ones stay here with a terminal status so they never resurface as 'new'. posted_days_ago is relative to 'last_refreshed' below - re-run a search rather than hand-adjusting it.
source_note: Pulled from Indeed on 2026-09-03 across 6 searches: EEG technologist trainee (Hollywood), neurodiagnostic technologist (Miami), EEG technician (Fort Lauderdale), EEG (Miami), behavioral health technician (Hollywood), psychiatric technician (Miami), clinical research coordinator neurology (Fort Lauderdale). The two purely neurodiagnostic searches returned zero results - South Florida is thin on EEG trainee postings right now. SECOND PASS via ZipRecruiter, same searches: 34 EEG matches and 12 neurodiagnostic matches within 40-45 miles, including a Cleveland Clinic EEG Technician Apprentice in Weston and an EEG Technician at Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital in Hollywood. Indeed returned zero for the identical queries. Never conclude the market is empty from one board. THIRD PASS 2026-09-03: read the actual qualifications from employer sources for the top three neuro roles. Result: Cleveland Clinic confirmed fully open to her (BLS is the only certification and she holds it); Memorial JDCH confirmed GATED behind an accredited ENDT program plus ABRET registry eligibility, so it was marked not_interested; Baptist Neurophysiology Tech Assistant confirmed to have no credential gate at all. Reading qualifications changed the ranking more than any scoring tweak has. FOURTH PASS: LinkedIn job-view pages (linkedin.com/jobs/view/<id>) are readable without a login via WebFetch. Stacey can paste any LinkedIn job URL and the full qualifications can be read from it. This removes the need for any LinkedIn scraper or MCP integration for reading postings. FIFTH PASS: LinkedIn's guest job search (linkedin.com/jobs/search?keywords=...) enumerated 60 Florida neurodiagnostic postings with their job IDs, all without a login. Each ID is then readable at /jobs/view/<id>. This is the full LinkedIn pipeline, no MCP or scraper required.

listings.title: Neurology Technician
listings.description: The Neurologic Wellness Institute in Boca Raton, FL is looking for a Full-Time Neurology Technician to join our team. Our ideal candidate is a self-starter, professional, punctual, and reliable. Benefits: We offer many great benefits, including PTO and Quarterly Bonus. Responsibilities: Reports to Lead Clinician and Clinical Director. Perform daily opening and closing procedures including cleaning and turning on equipment and lights. Perform patient diagnostics. Document intake history and examination for lead clinician. Upload diagnostics to EHR system. Assist in patient therapies and documentation in EHR. Clean and put away all exam and treatment equipment. Ensure that the treatment and restroom areas remain calm, welcoming, and clean. Uphold the positive reputation of our office by always treating visitors in a friendly, welcoming, and compassionate manner. Abide by all office policies and procedures. Preferred Skills/Abilities: Strong people/communication and development skills. Electronic Health Records knowledge. Experience in a Medical Clinic or Therapy Clinic. Education and Experience: Associate's degree or job-related vocational training. Benefits: Paid time off. Work Location: In person.
listings.notes: Closest thing to a neuro-diagnostic role currently posted in her range. 'Perform patient diagnostics' at a neurology practice is the door. Education bar is an associate's degree - she has a BS in Neuroscience, so she is over it. No pay published; ask on the call. Boca Raton is roughly a 40-minute drive from Hollywood.

listings.notes: This is the building where she did her Miami Summer Scholars psychiatry rotation in 2018 - neuropsych assessments, therapeutic interviewing, shadowing psychiatrists in outpatient clinics. She can say that in the first line of her cover letter. Salary floor is about $21.80/hr with a full hospital benefits package. Night shift is the standard way in.

listings.title: EEG Technologist Apprentice
listings.description: EEG Technologist Apprentice, Cleveland Clinic Florida, Weston FL. Full-time. QUALIFICATIONS VERIFIED FROM THE EMPLOYER'S OWN POSTING: High School Diploma or GED required. Knowledge of physical and biological sciences normally attained through high school coursework with emphasis in those areas. Knowledge of medical terminology preferred. Basic Life Support (BLS) certification required, or obtained within one month of hire. No prior EEG experience required and NO ABRET registration required on hire. Paid training and instruction provided in performing electroencephalographic examinations and epilepsy monitoring: calibrating and adjusting equipment, observing patients with video and digital recording equipment, applying electrodes, respiration monitors and EKG, obtaining relevant patient information from clinical records and questioning. The apprenticeship prepares you for the ABRET Registered EEG Technologist exam. Initial training runs 8-12 weeks on 1st shift 7:30am-4:00pm Monday-Friday, or nights 11pm-7:30am Sunday-Thursday. Candidates are recommended to submit a current resume with full work history.
listings.notes:
QUALIFICATIONS CHECKED AGAINST HER CV LINE BY LINE. She clears every single one:
  - HS diploma or GED -> she has a BS in Neuroscience and Psychology.
  - Science coursework -> Neuroscience major, plus PCR, ELISA and cell culture.
  - Medical terminology (preferred) -> two research assistantships and 70 clinical shadowing hours.
  - BLS certification -> HELD, confirmed 2026-09-03. Meets it outright, no one-month grace needed.
  - No registration required. They train you and prepare you for the ABRET exam.
There is no gap between her and this job. Apply today. Attach the full CV, not the short Indeed resume, because the work history is what they explicitly ask for. Both shift options are workable; the night shift is usually the easier one to get hired into.

listings.title: EEG Technician - FT - Days - JDCH
listings.description: EEG Technician, full-time days, Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital, Memorial Healthcare System, Hollywood FL. QUALIFICATIONS VERIFIED FROM THE EMPLOYER'S POSTING: No prior work experience required, BUT candidate must be a graduate of, or currently enrolled in, an accredited Electroneurodiagnostic technology program, and must be ABRET Registry Eligible. Prior EEG experience preferred. Duties include long-term video EEG monitoring, proficiency in the International 10-20 system, following ASET guidelines for EEG and long term neurodiagnostic monitoring in epilepsy, identifying and correcting artifacts, and editing and forwarding results to the attending physician. 8-10 hour days, 4-5 days per week, weekend on-call required. No training program offered to candidates outside an accredited ENDT program.
listings.notes:
CHECKED AND RULED OUT, which is the correct outcome. 'No prior work experience required' reads like an open door, but the next line requires enrollment in an accredited Electroneurodiagnostic technology program AND ABRET Registry Eligibility. She has neither, and there is no path in without them. This is exactly the kind of posting she asked to stop seeing.
KEEP THE EMPLOYER IN MIND ANYWAY: it is in Hollywood, her own city, and it is the same department as the $10K sign-on Registered Neurodiagnostic Technologist req. Finish the Cleveland Clinic apprenticeship and this becomes the obvious next move in about two years.

listings.title: Neurophysiology Tech Assistant, Neurophysiology Office, FT
listings.description: Neurophysiology Tech Assistant, Neurophysiology Office, Baptist Health South Florida, Miami FL. Full-time, 8:00am to 4:30pm. QUALIFICATIONS VERIFIED FROM THE EMPLOYER'S POSTING: High School Diploma or equivalent required. Minimum one year of experience as a Neurophysiology Tech Assistant or in a related field. NO registration, licence or ABRET credential required. Assists in performing neurophysiological procedures including EEGs, evoked potentials and intraoperative monitoring. Requires excellent interpersonal, organizational and communication skills to provide patient care.
listings.notes:
No credential gate at all, which makes it one of the few genuinely open doors into a neurophysiology department. The one-year 'related field' requirement is arguable in her favour: two research assistantships, 70 documented clinical shadowing hours, and two years of direct elderly resident care. Say 'related field' explicitly in the application.
Weekday 8-4:30 hours, which is rare in neurodiagnostics and much easier to build a life around than rotating nights. ZipRecruiter listed the band as $32k-$38.7k; Baptist's own market data for the title runs $20.56-$41.15/hr, so the posted floor may be low. Ask.

listings.title: EEG Technician - FT - Days - MRH
listings.description: EEG Technician, full-time, Memorial Regional Hospital (MRH), Memorial Healthcare System, Hollywood FL. QUALIFICATIONS VERIFIED FROM THE POSTING: High School Diploma or Equivalent (Required). Graduate of or enrolled in an Electro-neuro-diagnostic technology program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs (CAAHEP), or a clinically equivalent program. ABRET Registry Eligible. No prior work experience required. Someone with EMU and LTM monitoring experience highly preferred. Duties: attaching electrodes, reviewing patient history, educating patients, monitoring conditions, identifying artifacts, forwarding results to physicians, long-term video EEG monitoring, data retrieval and reduction. Proficiency in the International 10-20 system and ASET neurodiagnostic monitoring guidelines required. Rotating weekends. Shift listed as nights in the body despite 'Days' in the title. No training offered to candidates outside an accredited program.
listings.notes:
Stacey found this herself searching 'eeg apprentice' on LinkedIn. It is NOT an apprenticeship. It is Memorial Regional Hospital, a second Memorial site distinct from the Joe DiMaggio req already on file, and it carries the identical gate: CAAHEP-accredited Electroneurodiagnostic program plus ABRET Registry Eligibility. 'No prior work experience required' is again the line that makes it look open when it is not.
Two useful facts from it anyway: Memorial is actively hiring EEG techs at two sites in her own city within three weeks of each other, so the local demand is real; and the title says Days while the body says Nights, so verify the shift on any Memorial req before accepting.

listings.title: Monitor Technician I - Neurological/Stroke - FT Days - MRH
listings.description: Monitor Technician I, Neurological/Stroke unit, full-time days, Memorial Regional Hospital, Memorial Healthcare System, Hollywood FL. QUALIFICATIONS VERIFIED FROM THE POSTING: Vocational technical Electrocardiogram Competency required. BLS American Heart Association certification required. Monitor Technician certification required. ECG/EKG competency with successful completion of interpretation coursework. Minimum six months of experience required after completion of the Monitor Technician Extern program, or equivalent alternative experience. TRAINING PATHWAY STATED EXPLICITLY: 'New Hires minimum of six (6) months experience required: If incumbent has no prior work experience, they will be placed in the Monitor Technician - Extern role.' Responsibilities: continuous cardiac rhythm monitoring and surveillance, identifying arrhythmias and patient deterioration, attaching electrodes for ECG monitoring, documenting tracings, correcting artifacts, activating emergency response for cardiac events. No registration or licence required.
listings.notes:
THE STRATEGIC PLAY, and the most useful thing found today after Cleveland Clinic.
The posting states outright that a candidate with no prior work experience is placed in the Monitor Technician EXTERN role. That is a built-in on-ramp, in writing, from an employer who will otherwise not touch her.
  - BLS required -> she has it.
  - No ABRET, no accredited program, no licence.
  - ECG competency is coursework, and the extern route is how you get it.
  - Neurological/Stroke unit at Memorial Regional, in Hollywood, her own city. Day shift.
WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE JOB: Memorial has posted three EEG roles in three weeks that all gate behind a CAAHEP program she is not in. Getting inside Memorial on the neuro floor makes her an internal candidate, and internal transfer is the normal way people cross into EEG without going back to school. It is electrode work, artifact correction and waveform reading, which is genuinely adjacent to EEG rather than a detour.
Apply to this one AND to Cleveland Clinic. They are not competing; they are two different routes to the same place.

listings.title: Polysomnographic Technician I (Full Time, Nights)
listings.description: Polysomnographic Technician I, full-time nights, Nicklaus Children's Health System, Miami FL. QUALIFICATIONS VERIFIED FROM THE POSTING: Minimum 2 years of experience doing sleep studies. CPR Healthcare Provider certification, maintained active and in good standing throughout employment. No RPSGT or ABRET registration explicitly required, and no training offered to candidates without experience. Responsibilities: performing polysomnograms, CPAP studies and MSLT procedures per American Academy guidelines, preparing the sleep laboratory and calibrating instruments, diagnosing and correcting minor equipment malfunctions, patient hook-up to sensor equipment, scoring and report preparation within three days, equipment maintenance and inventory, emergency response, electronic medical record documentation.
listings.notes:
Nicklaus Children's is the lead she has been waiting on since her Notion planning page ('until Nicklaus calls back'). Worth knowing they are actively hiring.
This particular req is not hers: 'Technician I' sounds entry-level but it demands a minimum of two years doing sleep studies. Blocked by experience, not by a credential, so no amount of training language would rescue it.
USE IT ANYWAY: Nicklaus also has an EEG/LTM Tech III posted. Two open neurodiagnostic reqs at one hospital means a real department with turnover. If she has any contact there, this is the moment to ask what their entry-level or trainee pathway looks like. Set an alert on their careers page.

listings.title: Pharmacy Technician / Pharm Tech Apprenticeship
listings.description: Pharmacy Technician / Pharm Tech Apprenticeship at Walgreens, Miami FL. Full-time, $16.50-$20.00 per hour. QUALIFICATIONS VERIFIED FROM THE POSTING: Fluency in reading, writing and speaking English. Willingness to work flexible schedules including evenings and weekends. Preferred only: six months retail experience, prior Walgreens work, strong math skills, computer proficiency, inventory control knowledge, PTCB certification. Includes the Walgreens 'earn while you learn' Pharmacy Technician Training Program, recognised by ASHP and the Department of Labor. Training prepares candidates for PTCB certification and requires no prior pharmacy experience. No degree, licence or registration required. Duties: assisting pharmacists under direct supervision, processing prescriptions, customer service and patient engagement, cash register, inventory and stock, insurance claims, assisting with clinical services and sample collection.
listings.notes:
LEGITIMATE, AND ALSO THE WRONG CREDENTIAL FOR HER.
It is a genuine Department of Labor and ASHP recognised paid apprenticeship, no experience needed, posted 12 hours ago, and it ends in a real portable certification (PTCB). Nothing about it is a scam and she would very likely get it.
But the whole point of this board is a credential that compounds toward psychiatry. PTCB does not. It qualifies her to be a pharmacy technician. Meanwhile Cleveland Clinic's EEG apprenticeship pays roughly $25/hr against this one's $16.50-$20, requires nothing she lacks, and ends in ABRET - the credential that actually opens neuro and epilepsy monitoring work.
TAKE IT ONLY IF: the EEG applications go quiet for a couple of months and she needs income with a credential attached rather than a dead-end job. It beats retail. It does not beat the plan.
